# Global supporting cuts realize projective erosions with exact contact costs

This is a constructive arbitrary-base improvement over the sufficient
one-input DAG propagation. It does not prove a cap-payment inequality.
There is no recursive amplification: one intersects the actual fiber
hull with convex cuts extending the prescribed source erosion. Only
fibers sharing an original global supporting plane incur first cost.
Several sources share physical costs through a maximum.

Throughout d>=1. Let P be a nonempty finite lattice-complete subset of
Z^n, and let the positive compact convex fibers K_z obey every anchored
Minkowski inclusion. Let C be their convex hull in aff(P) times R^d.
Its integer fibers are exactly the K_z. No general position is used.

## 1. Continuous global supporting slopes at a prescribed fiber

Fix p in P and write h_z(u)=h_(K_z)(u), for unit continuous normals u.
There is a bounded continuous choice A_p(u) in R^n such that

    h_z(u) <= h_p(u)+A_p(u).(z-p)       for every z in P.       (1)

Indeed, at each u the finite linear inequality system is feasible by
Farkas' lemma. An infeasibility certificate would be numbers lambda_z>=0
with sum lambda_z(z-p)=0 and sum lambda_z(h_z-h_p)>0. Normalizing their
positive sum gives an anchored convex representation of p, contradicting
the support inequality for the given Minkowski inclusion.

Choose the unique minimum-Euclidean-norm feasible vector. We give the
continuity detail instead of assuming a continuous selection. For a
fixed finite constraint matrix V with rows z-p, its minimum-norm solution
to V A>=c is a nonnegative combination of active row vectors. This is
the elementary normal-cone optimality condition for a Euclidean
projection onto a polyhedron. A minimal such conic representation uses
linearly independent rows: any dependence permits subtraction of a
multiple of that dependence until a nonnegative coefficient vanishes.
For an independent active row set I its value is therefore

    A=V_I^T (V_I V_I^T)^(-1)c_I.                           (2)

The zero solution is the additional empty-row possibility. There are
finitely many such linear formulas. If feasible c_j converge to feasible
c, the associated solutions are bounded by these formulas. Pass to a
subsequence with the same I. Its coefficients
(V_I V_I^T)^(-1)(c_j)_I are nonnegative, so their limits are nonnegative;
the limit is feasible, the selected equalities stay active, and the same
normal-cone condition proves minimum norm at c. Uniqueness identifies
every subsequential limit. Thus the selection is continuous on the
feasible parameter domain. Apply this to the continuous support data in
(1); compactness of the normal sphere gives boundedness.

Any other bounded continuous feasible selection may instead be used.
The slopes are inequalities in the ORIGINAL integer coordinates; no
affine transformation of the lattice has taken place.

## 2. Exact global convex cuts

Choose finitely many prescribed interior sources (p_i,y_i), with their
ordinary projective normalizers a_i and globally finite positive convex
tangent extensions f_i from the projective boundary-potential theorem.
Write

    H_i(u)=h_(K_(p_i)-y_i)(u)>0.

Choose an arbitrary continuous b_i:S^(d-1)->R^n. For z in P define

    Phi_(i,z)(u,x)=H_i(u)
       f_i(1+a_i.(x-y_i)+b_i(u).(z-p_i)),
    Delta_(i,z)(u)=h_(p_i)(u)+A_(p_i)(u).(z-p_i)-h_z(u)>=0.

For small epsilon>=0 let C_epsilon be C intersected with ALL cuts

    u.x-A_(p_i)(u).(z-p_i)+epsilon Phi_(i,z)(u,x)
          <=h_(p_i)(u),               for every i and unit u.       (3)

Here z in (3) ranges over real base coordinates: Phi is defined by the
same displayed affine argument there. Each left side is convex in
(z,x), since H_i(u)>0 and f_i is convex. Thus C_epsilon is compact and
convex, and it is nested as epsilon grows. Its fiber at each z in P is
EXACTLY

    L_z(epsilon)={x in K_z:
       u.x+epsilon Phi_(i,z)(u,x)<=h_z(u)+Delta_(i,z)(u)
                                      for every i,u}.             (4)

For an interior o_z of K_z choose r_z>0 with o_z+r_z B subset K_z.
All fields in (4) are uniformly bounded by some M on the finitely many
original fibers and normal spheres. If t=epsilon M/r_z, then
o_z+(1-t)(K_z-o_z) satisfies (4): its unperturbed support slack is at
least t r_z in every direction, and the additional Delta is nonnegative.
For small epsilon all these inner homothets are positive. Consequently
every base in P remains occupied, and the projection of C_epsilon is
exactly conv(P). There are no other integer bases. This is an actual
compatible deformation, with no separate contact-repair argument.

With a single source, its p_i fiber is exactly the prescribed projective
gauge erosion. Indeed Delta_(i,p_i)=0 and b_i(u).(p_i-p_i)=0; its cuts
are precisely the all-normal inequalities defining that erosion. With
several sources each prescribed erosion is retained as a containing
constraint on its source fiber; other sources may remove extra mass.

If aff(P) is deficient in R^n, a fixed sufficiently small orthogonal
thickening in its rational perpendicular space supplies a full ambient
convex body with exactly these integer fibers. The projection of Z^n
to that perpendicular space is discrete (its matrix is rational), so
the thickening radius can be chosen below its nonzero lattice gap.
This is the same explicit rank repair as in the arbitrary-base DAG
source; it is not an assertion of containment in an original ambient C.

## 3. Actual first cost is a contact maximum

At a regular boundary point x of K_z let u_z(x) be its unique outward
unit normal. Define the physical speed

    v_z(x)=max( {Phi_(i,z)(u_z(x),x):
                  Delta_(i,z)(u_z(x))=0} union {0}).              (5)

This bounded measurable function need not be continuous in the normal.
Its discontinuity at a contact boundary is harmless; (5) follows from
the actual cuts, not an unsupported continuous-field approximation.
The total first loss is exactly

    |K_z|-|L_z(epsilon)|=epsilon integral_(boundary K_z) v_z dS
                              +o(epsilon).                      (6)

Here is a direct nonsmooth proof. Use radial coordinates centered at
o_z. At an old radial endpoint x put x_t=o_z+(1-t)(x-o_z), and let
t_epsilon be its fractional radial loss. The inner homothet above
gives 0<=t_epsilon<=O(epsilon) uniformly. At any active old constraint
with Delta=0 and u supporting at x, (4) gives

    t_epsilon u.(x-o_z) >=epsilon Phi_(i,z)(u,x_t).

Thus the lower limit of t_epsilon/epsilon is at least the maximum of
Phi/(u.(x-o_z)) over those old active constraints. Conversely, whenever
t_epsilon>0 the new endpoint is interior to the old body and some cut
is active; compactness of the finite source set and normal sphere
supplies convergent active indices along any sequence. Its old slack
h_z(u)-u.x+Delta is nonnegative and O(epsilon), so the limiting normal
supports x and has Delta=0. The active equality, after discarding that
nonnegative old slack, gives the matching upper bound. At a regular x
the normal is unique and its radial support denominator is positive,
at least r_z. Therefore

    t_epsilon/epsilon -> v_z(x)/(u_z(x).(x-o_z)).          (7)

Convex boundaries are regular surface-almost everywhere. The radial
Jacobian is u_z(x).(x-o_z), so radial dominated convergence turns (7)
into (6). The uniform inner-homothet estimate is the domination. In
d=1 the two radial endpoints and H_0 boundary measure give the same
argument directly.

For any fixed ambient closed halfspace H let kappa_(z,H) be its actual
inward loss selector on K_z: 1 on an entirely captured fiber, 0 when
its interior is disjoint from H, and 1_(int H_z) on a proper cut.
The same radial proof gives

    mu(H)-mu_epsilon(H)
        =epsilon sum_z integral kappa_(z,H) v_z dS+o(epsilon).   (8)

The cutting hyperplane of a proper cut meets the old boundary in surface
measure zero; an inside
supporting trace loses all its removed mass, and an outside supporting
trace loses none. Purely integer halfspaces retain the full/empty
closed-boundary rule. Thus no supporting facet is assigned a fictitious
loss by using its closed indicator. Finite menus have uniform little-o
errors simply because they are finite.

## 4. Prescribed source credit and the remaining quantitative issue

For every source i, Delta_(i,p_i) vanishes in EVERY direction and (5)
dominates its own projective boundary potential. If D_i is that
PRESCRIBED potential's positive total cost, every ambient halfspace
containing (p_i,y_i) consequently loses at least Gamma_d D_i on that
fiber to first order. This statement does not replace D_i by the larger
final source cost when other prescribed sources also act there.

All other costs and cap credits are exactly (5)--(8), and coincide on
shared physical boundary through a maximum. Their total is not bounded
by the number of sources or occupied parities. A fixed critical cover
strictly descends precisely under the sufficient row tests

    sum_z integral (kappa_(z,H)-beta) v_z dS >0

for every critical row of that cover; its slack rows persist. This
construction does not prove those tests can always be met.

The new freedoms are concrete: choose the feasible supporting slope
A_i(u), the affine base denominator shift b_i(u), and the actual
critical circuits. A chosen slope exposes only its true global contact
fibers; strictly slack fibers contribute zero first cost automatically.
This differs from making one input fund every anchored relation via
recursive worst-partner suprema. Exact ambient convex intersection
already enforces all relations here.
